newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops fortify in captured rebel areas.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops fortify in captured rebel areas.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops were fortifying positions in northern areas captured from separatist Tamil Tiger rebels after fierce fighting last week, the Defence Ministry said on Monday.
"Troops continue to consolidate in the captured areas of Nedunkeni and north of Omanthai," a ministry statement said.

Troops on the offensive wrestled control of Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of Vavuniya and northeastern Nedunkeni, about 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vavuniya, from Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels last week.

Military officials in the north told Reuters that security forces were building bunkers and forward defence lines north and northeast of government-held Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
"More security personnel have been sent to these areas to secure the places taken by the military," one official said.
Intelligence and police sources said the battlefront was relatively quiet on Monday after last week's fierce fighting.

The multi-pronged offensive launched last week, codenamed "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", has so far managed to carve fresh inroads into the LTTE's northern Wanni heartland, a Defence Ministry official told Reuters.
"Troops have managed to capture and control land where no government soldier has stepped on for many years," he said.

The LTTE, fighting a 13-year-old war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, control vast swathes of land in the mostly shrub-covered Wanni in the island's north.

Defence Ministry officials have said that some 250 rebels had been killed since the offensive began and that two divisions were moving on separate flanks, trying to open a land supply route linking Vavuniya with Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north.
Jaffna, the rebels' former stronghold and the capital of their would-be homeland, is under government control.

"We estimate about 250 terrorists have been killed in the operation," military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga told Reuters on Sunday. "Enemy transmissions monitored by the army indicate 316 cadres have been wounded."
The rebels have accused the army of killing Tamil civilians and destroying property under the pretext of opening up a supply route, and of routinely exaggerating rebel casualties.
According to figures released by the army, 42 soldiers have been killed so far in the offensive. But newspaper reports put the toll at 70, including some officers.
Hospital sources said some 320 soldiers have been wounded.
The clandestine Voice of Tigers radio, monitored by Reuters, said on Monday that the Sri Lankan navy had increased patrolling the Palk Straits, which separates the island from India.

It said the army was still firing shells in the Wanni region and fighting was continuing. "Nedunkeni has become a ghost town after virtually all Tamil residents -- now homeless -- were bombed out of their houses by persistent air and ground attacks", an overnight LTTE statement said.
Journalists have not yet been allowed in the battle zone.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, but the rebels say the toll is higher.
